comparator.name: Bachelor Electrical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: TU/e's current official programme, degree-structure and Education Guide pages, checked 2026-10-03, describe a three-year, 180-EC Electrical Engineering bachelor for students starting in 2023-2024 or later. The degree comprises 120 EC of electrical-engineering major and Bachelor College core formation, including challenge-based projects and the Bachelor Final Project, plus a 60-EC elective part consisting of a 15-EC Impact of Technology learning line and 45 EC of electives. The complete 120/15/45 allocation is retained below rather than assigning unsupported individual credit values to the current programme page's topic and course lists.
components: Electrical Engineering major and Bachelor College core programme, including Bachelor Final Project

Compulsory formation in calculus, linear algebra, probability, programming, circuits, electronics, digital systems, electromagnetic fields, signals and systems, communication, control, embedded systems, electrical energy, measurement, challenge-based engineering and the Bachelor Final Project.
Genuine programme choice within the official elective part.
Genuine elective space preserved from the official curriculum structure.

exception.reason: Electrical Engineering at TU/e is a cumulative engineering degree built around electrical and electromagnetic theory, analogue and digital circuits, electronic devices, signal processing, communication, control, embedded systems, measurement, electrical-energy conversion and distribution, engineering laboratories and challenge-based hardware projects before a discipline-specific Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers relevant mathematics, programming, data science, AI, robotics, linear systems, renewable-energy systems and consumer-product design. It does not offer the compulsory electromagnetics, circuit and electronics sequence, semiconductor-device formation, measurement and instrumentation laboratories, communication-hardware sequence, electrical machines and power-electronics progression, embedded-hardware laboratories or integrated electrical-engineering project spine. A 24-course UCR response would be a mathematics-and-computing programme with energy and robotics applications, not a defensible Electrical Engineering comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official current structure accounts for all 180 EC as 120 EC of Electrical Engineering major and Bachelor College core formation, including the Bachelor Final Project, a 15-EC Impact of Technology learning line and 45 EC of electives. The programme's compulsory formation progresses from mathematics, programming and physical foundations through circuit analysis, analogue and digital electronics, electromagnetic fields, signals and systems, communication, control, embedded and connected devices, sensing and measurement, electrical-energy generation, conversion and distribution, semiconductor technology, engineering design and challenge-based projects. The programme presents these domains as an integrated hardware-and-software engineering formation rather than as optional applications of mathematics or computing.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH213 Computational & Numerical Methods, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH312 Linear Systems and DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics provide useful quantitative foundations. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISCOMP211 Networks & Operating Systems, DISCOMP213 Software Development, DISDATA111 Introduction to Data Science, DISDATA211 Machine Learning, DISDATA212 Image Processing & Computer Vision, DISDATA311 Neural Networks & Deep Learning and DISDATA312 Robotics provide relevant computation, signal-adjacent analysis, perception and control applications. ENSGATE101 Sustainability Essentials I, ENSSUST211 Energy & Sustainability and ENSSUST311 Renewable System Design add energy-system context, while BENENTR111 Consumer Product Design adds team-based product development and prototyping. The workbook nevertheless contains no dedicated electricity-and-magnetism sequence, circuit theory, analogue or digital electronics, semiconductor physics and devices, electrical measurements and instrumentation laboratory, radio-frequency or communication hardware, electrical machines, power electronics, embedded-hardware design, computer architecture or integrated electrical-engineering laboratory and capstone sequence. DISMATH312 studies mathematical linear systems but cannot replace circuits, electronics, signals laboratories and control implementation. DISDATA312 covers general robotics rather than the target's staged hardware, sensing, embedded-control and electrical design formation. The available UCR courses therefore support intelligent systems or sustainable-energy themes while leaving the defining electrical-engineering spine unmatched.
